venture.name: Hockey Bag with Built-in Stick Holders (working concept; no separate brand name provided)
venture.business_concept: A hockey equipment bag with built-in external stick holders intended to reduce the number of loose items players and families carry to the rink.
venture.primary_product: Full-size hockey equipment bag with holders for at least two sticks (two-stick capacity is a stated product refinement in the venture workspace).
venture.target_customers: Youth hockey players, mainly ages 6–20, and their parents or caregivers who make or influence equipment purchases. The venture workspace describes a high-income demographic and later recommends promoting to parents.
customer_needs: Carry gear and sticks in fewer trips
Keep sticks together and identifiable on team transport
Reduce carrying discomfort and loose equipment
venture.value_proposition: Convenient transport by combining gear storage and at least two stick holders in one bag.
venture.geographic_market: North America, Europe, and Russia were listed; the workspace's market analysis recommends validating North America first and reassessing Russia against the high-income target.
features_documented: Holds at least two sticks (venture refinement)
assumptions_and_gaps: No separate business/brand name supplied; concept name used.
No dimensions, materials, gear capacity, manufacturing cost, or selling channel supplied.
The two-stick capacity and reinforced construction are intended features from the venture workspace, not a finished product specification.
venture.existing_research_context: Workspace reports a sample of 61 Ice Warehouse reviews across 15 hockey bag product pages. Its own analysis states carrying comfort appeared in 20 reviews and stick storage was rarely mentioned because conventional bags lack holders. These are the student's sample findings, not independently rechecked in this pricing mission.

currency_note: Prices are captured as displayed on the cited pages on the research date. USD and EUR are kept separate; no exchange-rate conversion is used.

competitors.name: BAUER
competitors.geographic_market: North America; brand also sells internationally
competitors.target_customers: Ice hockey players and families, including youth and adult players
competitors.main_products: Ice hockey equipment and bags, including carry bags and stick bags
competitors.positioning: Established mainstream performance hockey brand; broad equipment assortment
competitors.differentiating_features: Premium carry bag has a large main compartment, end pockets, ventilation panels, and external water bottle pocket.
competitors.reason_for_inclusion: A recognizable full-equipment carry bag is a realistic substitute for the venture's gear-storage function, although it does not integrate stick holders.

competitors.name: Pacific Rink
competitors.geographic_market: United States and Canada; ships internationally according to its site
competitors.target_customers: Ice hockey players and families seeking specialized, organized bags; youth and smaller players have a junior option
competitors.main_products: Premium hockey player bags, junior player bags, backpacks, and stick bags
competitors.differentiating_features: Player Bag lists 1000D nylon, reinforced ballistic-nylon bottom, wet mesh bag, skate sleeves, organization pockets, hideaway backpack straps, and YKK zippers.
competitors.reason_for_inclusion: Specialized gear bags compete directly for the same equipment-carrying purchase, and its junior size is relevant to youth players; no integrated stick holder was identified on the cited pages.

competitors.name: CCM
competitors.geographic_market: North America and international hockey markets
competitors.target_customers: Ice hockey players, including youth players needing stick transport
competitors.main_products: Hockey equipment and separate stick bags
competitors.positioning: Mainstream hockey equipment brand; affordable, functional accessory offering
competitors.differentiating_features: CCM 74-inch stick bag listing specifies heavy-duty polyester, carry strap, and capacity for two sticks.
competitors.reason_for_inclusion: A two-stick bag solves the stick-transport part of the problem at a low price, but requires a second bag alongside the gear bag.

competitors.name: Warrior
competitors.geographic_market: North America and international hockey markets
competitors.target_customers: Ice hockey players and teams; individual players needing stick transport
competitors.main_products: Hockey equipment, individual stick bags, team bags, and player bags
competitors.positioning: Performance hockey brand with individual and team equipment options
competitors.differentiating_features: Official Pro Hockey Stick Bag page lists heavy-duty vinyl zipper, reinforced stitching, nylon straps, clear ID pocket, and capacity up to three senior sticks.
competitors.reason_for_inclusion: Its individual stick bag and broader hockey bag line are alternatives for the separate-stick-carrying problem; no combined gear-and-stick holder product was verified.

competitors.name: TK Sports
competitors.target_customers: Field hockey players, teams, and active consumers
competitors.main_products: Field hockey equipment and bags, including P7 Duffle Bag
competitors.positioning: Purpose-designed hockey equipment with feature-oriented mid-market positioning
competitors.differentiating_features: P7 is a 50 L duffle with integrated stick holder, hidden backpack straps, detachable padded shoulder strap, four storage compartments, detachable shoe bag, and water-repellent 600D ripstop fabric.
competitors.reason_for_inclusion: It is the closest verified product-feature analogue because it integrates a stick holder into a hockey duffle; it serves field hockey, not the venture's ice-hockey market, so its price is not treated as directly comparable.

price_comparison.comparison_definition: Only listed USD prices for full ice-hockey equipment bags with a complete gear-storage function. Separate stick bags and the field-hockey TK P7 are excluded. The subset contains Bauer Premium Carry Bag S24 ($109.99), Pacific Rink Junior Player Bag ($195.99), and Pacific Rink Player Bag ($239.99). Prices are per bag, one-time purchases, before shipping/tax.
price_comparison.caveat: This is a small, selected benchmark set with different sizes and feature levels; it is descriptive, not a market-wide price estimate. It does not represent integrated-holder products in the ice hockey category because none were verified in this research sample.

preliminary_pricing_recommendation.rationale: An initial North American range of $119-$149 would sit modestly above the observed $109.99 Bauer carry bag and below Pacific Rink's $195.99 junior and $239.99 full-size premium bags. The integrated two-stick holders and reinforced high-wear areas could support that premium over a basic carry bag if design quality and durability are validated. Product costs, demand, channel margins, and willingness to pay are unknown, so this is a test range rather than a final or optimal price.
most_relevant_benchmarks: BAUER Premium Carry Bag S24 for mainstream full-bag comparison
Pacific Rink Junior Player Bag for youth segment and premium specialized bag comparison
TK P7 Duffle for integrated-stick-holder feature analogy, with field-hockey caveat
uncertainties: No production cost or margin data
No verified integrated-holder ice-hockey competitor in this sample
Cross-market taxes, freight, currencies, and purchasing power differ

research_limitations: Feature and price sample is not exhaustive and is not a statistically representative market sample.
The student's source venture document is pasted workspace text; the separate business name, intended distribution channel, final specs, and product cost are not available.
No price for a directly comparable ice-hockey bag with integrated stick holders was verified.
Warrior price comes from a retailer category listing and was only partially verified; stick-bag prices are not comparable to full equipment bags.
Price comparisons exclude tax and shipping unless noted. No currency conversion was made.
Student venture consumer-review findings are reported as prior workspace findings and were not independently reanalyzed here.
